hook.en: A giant wheel at the Dasara exhibition turns at a steady speed, yet every seat is accelerating all the time. How can that be?
hook.kn: ದಸರಾ ವಸ್ತುಪ್ರದರ್ಶನದ ಜೈಂಟ್ ವೀಲ್ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಜವದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೂ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಆಸನವೂ ಸದಾ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ಹೇಗೆ?

narration.en: A giant wheel at the Dasara exhibition turns at a steady speed, yet every seat is accelerating all the time. How can that be?
narration.kn: ದಸರಾ ವಸ್ತುಪ್ರದರ್ಶನದ ಜೈಂಟ್ ವೀಲ್ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಜವದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೂ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಆಸನವೂ ಸದಾ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ಹೇಗೆ?

body.en: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of the velocity keeps changing, so there is an acceleration. It points towards the centre and has magnitude $a_c = v^2/R$. This is the centripetal (centre-seeking) acceleration. Its direction keeps changing, so it is not a constant vector.
body.kn: ಏಕರೂಪ ವರ್ತುಲ ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜವ ಸ್ಥಿರ, ಆದರೆ ವೇಗದ ದಿಕ್ಕು ಸದಾ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಕಡೆಗೆ v²/R ಪರಿಮಾಣದ ಕೇಂದ್ರಾಭಿಮುಖ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದರ ದಿಕ್ಕು ಬದಲಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ ಅದು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಸದಿಶವಲ್ಲ.

points.en: a_c is perpendicular to v at every instant

say.en: In uniform circular motion the speed stays the same, but the velocity keeps turning, always along the tangent.
The change in velocity points to the centre. So the acceleration is centripetal, of size v squared over R.
Angular speed is angle per second. Linear speed is omega R, and omega is two pi times the frequency.
Example: an insect in a groove of radius 12 centimetres makes 7 revolutions in 100 seconds.

narration.en: On the board: Why circular motion is accelerated.

body.en: Angular speed $\omega = \Delta\theta/\Delta t$ is measured in rad/s, and the linear speed is $v = \omega R$. The period T is the time for one revolution and the frequency is ν = 1/T, so $\omega = 2\pi\nu = 2\pi/T$ and $a_c = 4\pi^2\nu^2 R$.
body.kn: ಕೋನೀಯ ಜವ ω = Δθ/Δt (rad/s). ರೇಖೀಯ ಜವ v = ωR. ಆವರ್ತನಾವಧಿ T ಮತ್ತು ಆವರ್ತನ ν = 1/T; ω = 2πν = 2π/T.

narration.en: Angular speed $\omega = \Delta\theta/\Delta t$ is measured in rad/s, and the linear speed is $v = \omega R$. The period T is the time for one revolution and the frequency is ν = 1/T, so $\omega = 2\pi\nu = 2\pi/T$ and $a_c = 4\pi^2\nu^2 R$.
narration.kn: ಕೋನೀಯ ಜವ ω = Δθ/Δt (rad/s). ರೇಖೀಯ ಜವ v = ωR. ಆವರ್ತನಾವಧಿ T ಮತ್ತು ಆವರ್ತನ ν = 1/T; ω = 2πν = 2π/T.

problem.en: An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 cm moves steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 s. Find its angular speed, linear speed and acceleration.

steps.en: a = ω²R = 0.44² × 12 ≈ 2.3 cm/s², directed towards the centre.

body.en: On the same circle, doubling the speed makes the centripetal acceleration four times (a ∝ v²). At the same ω, doubling the radius doubles it (a ∝ R). At the same v, doubling the radius halves it.
